canonical_data: append-only session logs with content-addressed blobs, plus consolidated memory files and generated playbooks
strengths: Authenticates against subscriptions the developer already pays for across many providers, avoiding a second metered bill
Mutation is gated behind an approved plan, and the project ships no permission-bypass flag by design
Unattended runs are bounded by a lease that only real tool execution renews, so streaming text cannot keep a stalled run alive
weaknesses: The project declares itself experimental and pre-release and tells users to verify outputs before relying on them
Retrieval is keyword, structural, and language-server based, with no semantic or vector search documented
Automatic memory is disabled by default and its artifacts are private runtime state rather than a supported interface
why_it_matters: The clearest worked example of a coding agent designed around subscription authentication and asynchronous human approval rather than metered billing and terminal presence.
